I1.quote: High-pressure H2 adsorption measurements at 77 and 298 K were carried out using a volumetric Sieverts-type adsorption analyzer equipped with stainless-steel sample and reference cells.

I2.quote: Here, we address this porosity-packing density trade-off in carbon aerogels through a binderless densification strategy that preserves micro- and mesoporosity while substantially increasing bulk density.

I3.quote: in situDIW-printed monolith achieved H2 storage capacities of 1.8 wt % and 6.9 g/L at 298 K and 5.9 wt % and 36 g/L at 77 K, both at 100 bar

I4.quote: Quantitative textural analysis revealed that the pristine DACA sorbent possessed a remarkably high BET surface area of 2955 m2/g, indicative of its highly open porous network.

I5.quote: Hydrogen storage in porous carbons is fundamentally constrained by the trade-off between high porosity and efficient packing density, which limits achievable volumetric capacity.

notes: Original research article on densified double-activated carbon aerogels (DACA, DIW, in situDIW, cold/hot-pressed pellets); binders, fumed silica and HPMC are removed by pyrolysis/CO2 etching at 1000 C. Uptake is volumetric (Sieverts; SI Section S1 names BELSORP-HP), 0-100 bar at 77 and 298 K (Figures 8-9); reported values are 'total' uptake computed from measured excess (eqs S1-S4). BET areas for all seven measured samples in Table 1. The pristine DACA material comes from the authors' earlier work (ref 7), but the paper does not state that its H2 values were published before, so duplicate_data does not apply. Not retracted (record flag false; no retraction notice in PDF). Inconsistency noted: degassing before H2 measurement is 120 C for 12 h in main Section 3.4, but 150 C for 12 h (and 10 h) in SI Section S1.
